title: Mars Colonization, Starship, and Planetary Habitability
executive_summary: Mars colonization involves proposed human settlements on Mars, utilizing in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) to extract water, fuel, and oxygen from the Martian environment.
image_caption: Hubble Space Telescope view of Mars.

key_sections.title: In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU)
key_sections.content: The Sabatier reaction uses atmospheric CO2 and subsurface water ice on Mars to synthesize methane fuel and oxygen (CH4 + O2) for return rocket flights.

key_sections.title: Radiation Protection and Regolith Hazards
key_sections.content: Without a global magnetic field, Mars colonists require thick regolith shielding or underground lava tube habitats to block cosmic rays and solar particle events, while managing toxic perchlorate salts in Martian dust.

key_sections.title: SpaceX Starship Super Heavy Transportation
key_sections.content: SpaceX's fully reusable Starship rocket is designed to lift 100+ metric tons to orbit and refuel in space for deep space transport to Mars.
